meta.title: The black-spatula calculation
meta.note: Paraphrased excerpt; the published correction fixed this number.

flags.detail: Recomputed 420,000 ng/d, but the paper says 42,000. Off by exactly ×10: a decimal or unit slip.

explanations: Typo in the exposure value: the author may have intended 700 ng/kg bw/day instead of 7000 ng/kg bw/day, giving 60 kg × 700 = 42 000 ng/day.
Misplaced decimal point: an extra zero was omitted when transcribing the product (e.g., 420 000 written as 42 000).

Unit confusion: the body weight might have been entered in grams (60 g) rather than kilograms, leading to 0.06 kg × 7000 = 420 ng/day, which after a further conversion step could appear as 42 000 ng/day.
triage.check: Verify the original body weight and exposure concentration used in the calculation, redo the multiplication ensuring correct units (kg and ng/kg), and confirm whether any conversion factor (e.g., to µg) was applied before reporting the final value.

review.impact: Yes, if the reference intake is actually 420,000 ng/day, the estimated utensil-derived intake of 34,700 ng/day would represent only ~8% of the reference dose rather than 83%, substantially weakening the claim that exposure 'approaches the reference dose.'
review.author_query: We noticed the reference intake calculation (60 kg × 7000 ng/kg bw/day) yields 420,000 ng/day, but the paper states 42,000 ng/day. Could you confirm which value is correct and whether the 83% comparison should be updated accordingly?
